passages.¶1: Legend: check mark = present / defining; tilde = partial / possible; blank = absent / not required.
passages.¶10: Note 9: terminology varies across literature (empathic concern, Brown-style sympathy). Note 10: the five profile columns are ideal types on a dark-to-light spectrum; empath is not the moral ideal; altruist matches the Light Triad (Kaufman et al., 2019); integrated ideal alone scores well across every block. Note 11: the three Light Triad rows partly restate earlier rows; only Faith in Humanity adds a new dimension.
passages.¶2: The four component columns (cognitive and affective empathy, sympathy, compassion) sit left of the double rule. The five to the right are whole-person profiles, arranged darkest to lightest: psychopath, sociopath, empath, altruist, and the integrated ideal. Rows stay ordered by the two dark profiles' contrast, in four blocks separated by blank dividers: present in both, in the psychopath only, in the sociopath only, and in neither.
passages.¶3: Block present-in-both plus psychopath-only rows. Accurately modeling the other's mental state: cognitive check, affective partial, sympathy partial, compassion check; Psychopath check, Sociopath partial, Empath partial, Altruist check, Integrated check. Maintains self/other boundary: cognitive check, sympathy check, compassion check; Psychopath check, Sociopath partial, Altruist check, Integrated check. Can exist in manipulators / con artists: cognitive check only; Psychopath check, Sociopath partial. Controlled / instrumental rather than reactive / impulsive: cognitive check, sympathy partial, compassion check; Psychopath check, Altruist check, Integrated check.
passages.¶4: Block sociopath-only rows. Actually sharing / mirroring the emotion: affective check; Sociopath partial, Empath check, Altruist partial, Integrated check. Capacity to genuinely care about the person at all: affective partial, sympathy check, compassion check; Sociopath check, Empath check, Altruist check, Integrated check. Motivation to help or act: affective partial, sympathy partial, compassion check; Sociopath partial, Empath partial, Altruist check, Integrated check. Produces guilt / remorse after causing harm: affective partial, sympathy partial, compassion partial; Sociopath partial, Empath check, Integrated partial. Risk of emotional contagion and burnout: affective check, sympathy partial; Sociopath partial, Empath check, Integrated partial. Biased toward vivid, similar individuals: cognitive partial, affective check, sympathy partial; Sociopath check, Empath check, Integrated partial. Treats people as ends, not means (Kantianism): affective partial, sympathy partial, compassion check; Sociopath partial, Empath check, Altruist check, Integrated check. Values each person's dignity and worth (Humanism): affective partial, sympathy check, compassion check; Sociopath partial, Empath check, Altruist check, Integrated check.
passages.¶5: Block neither rows. Concern reaches beyond a vivid / similar in-group: sympathy partial, compassion check; Altruist check, Integrated check. Believes people are fundamentally good (Faith in Humanity): sympathy partial, compassion partial; Empath check, Altruist check, Integrated check. Sustainable and scalable as a moral guide: cognitive partial, sympathy partial, compassion check; Altruist check, Integrated check.
passages.¶6: Note 1: Sympathy gets tilde on modeling the other's mind because you can pity someone while badly misreading them. Note 2: Affective empathy gets tilde on capacity to care: contagion can happen involuntarily, without real concern. Note 3: The manipulators row is the sharpest diagnostic for the cognitive/affective split and the psychopath's signature; cognitive empathy alone is compatible with cruelty.
passages.¶7: Note 4: The sustainable and scalable row reflects the Bloom/Singer argument (Paul Bloom, Against Empathy, and Tania Singer's compassion-training research), which is a position, not a consensus; critics reply compassion without empathic grounding risks becoming abstract or paternalistic. Note 5: Boundary maintenance is the structural difference between affective empathy and everything else: merging drives its power, burnout, and bias.
passages.¶8: Note 6: the psychopath is close to the cognitive-empathy column standing alone; the sociopath is close to the affective-empathy and sympathy columns clamped to a narrow in-group and stripped of regulation; almost everything the psychopath has, the sociopath also has in degraded form, so cold instrumental control is the psychopath's one distinguishing possession.
passages.¶9: Note 7: Etiology is deliberately left out as a row: psychopathy is often theorized as innate, sociopathy as acquired; causes are not response shapes. Note 8: psychopath and sociopath are not formal diagnoses; both fall under Antisocial Personality Disorder and the split is contested; treat the columns as ideal types.

nodes.text: The matrix separates cognitive and affective empathy, sympathy, and compassion, then profiles psychopath, sociopath, empath, altruist, and integrated ideal.
Four components sit left of the double rule; five dark-to-light profiles sit right.
Rows fall in four blocks: present in both, psychopath only, sociopath only, neither.
Cognitive empathy means accurate modeling, boundary, and control; it survives in manipulators.
The psychopath column is essentially the cognitive-empathy column standing alone.
Sympathy earns only partial on modeling: pity can badly misread people.
Affective empathy means sharing emotion, with contagion, burnout, and vividness bias.
Affective empathy lacks boundary maintenance, unlike everything else in the table.
Affective empathy earns only partial on caring: contagion can occur without concern.
The sociopath resembles affective empathy plus sympathy clamped to an in-group, unregulated.
Compassion alone combines caring, motivation to help, wide scope, and sustainability.
Only compassion scores full marks on helping motivation and sustainable scalable guidance.
The Bloom and Singer pro-compassion case is a position, not a consensus.
The psychopath keeps only cold instrumental control; the sociopath holds the affective cluster.
Almost all psychopath traits recur degraded in sociopath; only control is psychopath-only.
Emotion-sharing, caring, helping, guilt, and contagion rows belong to sociopath, not psychopath.
The empath maximizes affect unregulated, so it is not the moral ideal.
The empath lights up sharing, contagion, and bias but fails boundary, scope, and scalability.
The altruist embodies compassion and the Light Triad: Kantianism, Humanism, Faith in Humanity.
The integrated ideal alone scores well across every block, opposing both dark profiles.
Kantianism inverts the manipulators row; only Faith in Humanity adds a new dimension.
The table limits its scope deliberately and treats dark columns as ideal types.
Etiology stays out: causal origin is not a response shape.
Psychopath and sociopath are not formal diagnoses; both fall under antisocial personality disorder.
Terminology varies; empathic concern and pop-psych sympathy differ from table usage.
